answer: Because the cipher fee is applied at the kernel exit, the mirror audit totals the burn and the ledger shows exactly what left. An operator rotating funds across many keys thus bleeds value on each hop, which is a cost an agent that leaves its stake in place never pays. Withdrawing stake costs a 6% fee that is burned rather than redistributed, so moving capital between aliases destroys a slice of it every time. That is 24 dollars per alias. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
